sections.title: Detailed Brief Overview
rows: **Continents and Oceans** form the primary **first-order relief features** of the Earth's surface.
Formed over **4.5 billion years** through planetary accretion, differentiation, and subsequent **plate tectonics**.
**Alfred Wegener** proposed the **Continental Drift Theory (1912)**; **Harry Hess** proposed **Sea Floor Spreading**.
Crucial for understanding **global climate systems**, **biodiversity distribution**, **geopolitics**, and **natural resources**.
**7 Continents** (Asia, Africa, North America, South America, Antarctica, Europe, Australia) and **5 Oceans** (Pacific, Atlantic, Indian, Southern, Arctic).
Continental landmasses categorized into **cratons, shields, and fold mountains**; Ocean basins divided into **continental shelves, slopes, abyssal plains, and trenches**.
High-yield static and conceptual questions in **UP Assistant Teacher (Environmental & Social Studies)** exam regarding highest peaks, deepest trenches, and strait/canal locations.
**Northern Hemisphere** contains about **60% of land** (Land Hemisphere); **Southern Hemisphere** contains about **81% water** (Water Hemisphere).

subcards.title: Continental Drift Theory (CDT)
content: Proposed by **Alfred Wegener** in **1912**.
All landmasses were once a single supercontinent named **Pangea**, surrounded by a mega-ocean named **Panthalassa**.
Pangea broke into **Lauratia** (Northern) and **Gondwanaland** (Southern) separated by the **Tethys Sea**.
Driving forces cited by Wegener: **Pole-fleeing force** (centrifugal force) and **Tidal force** (Sun and Moon).

subcards.title: Plate Tectonics Theory
content: Modern unifying theory replacing Wegener's drift mechanism.
Earth's lithosphere is broken into **7 major and several minor tectonic plates** floating on the **asthenosphere**.
Three types of plate boundaries: **Divergent** (constructive), **Convergent** (destructive), and **Transform** (conservative).
Explains the formation of **fold mountains, ocean trenches, mid-oceanic ridges, and island arcs**.

subcards.title: Sea Floor Spreading
content: Proposed by **Harry Hess** in **1961**.
New oceanic crust is continuously formed at **mid-oceanic ridges** through volcanic upwelling of magma.
Crust is destroyed or consumed at **deep oceanic trenches** through subduction zones.
Provided the mechanism that validated **Alfred Wegener's Continental Drift Theory**.

subcards.title: Relief Features of Ocean Basins
content: **Continental Shelf**: Shallow, gently sloping extension of continents; rich in **petroleum and fisheries**.
**Continental Slope**: Steep drop connecting the continental shelf to the deep ocean floor.
**Deep Sea Plain (Abyssal Plain)**: Vast, flat, sediment-covered areas covering the largest part of ocean basins.
**Oceanic Trenches**: Deepest parts of oceans, e.g., **Mariana Trench** in the Pacific Ocean.

subcards.title: Ocean Salinity and Temperature
content: Average global ocean salinity is **35 parts per thousand (ppt)**.
Highest salinity recorded in **Lake Van (Turkey)**, **Dead Sea**, and **Lake Assal (Djibouti)**.
Temperature of oceans decreases with **increasing depth**, marked by a thermocline layer.
Influenced by **evaporation, precipitation, ocean currents, and freshwater influx** from rivers.

sections.title: Important Facts and Data
rows: Contains highest mountain ranges, plateaus (**Pamir**), and largest lake (**Caspian Sea**).
Only continent crossed by **Equator, Tropic of Cancer, and Tropic of Capricorn**.
Famous for **Great Lakes**, Rocky Mountains, and Mississippi river system.
Contains **Amazon Rainforest**, Andes Mountains, and Atacama Desert.
Known as the **White Continent**, highest average elevation, and frozen desert.
Peninsula of peninsulas; highly indented coastline; bounded by Ural Mountains.
Known as the **Island Continent** and smallest continent entirely in Southern Hemisphere.

sections.title: Ocean Dimensions and Extremes
rows: Covers more area than all land combined; contains **Ring of Fire**.
**S-shaped** ocean; busiest commercial shipping route; has **Mid-Atlantic Ridge**.
Only ocean named after a country (**India**); experiences seasonal **monsoon reversals**.
Encircles Antarctica; bounded by the **Antarctic Convergence (60° S)**.
Surrounds North Pole; mostly ice-covered; connects to Atlantic via **Fram Strait**.

sections.title: Major Straits and Isthmuses
rows: Separates **Russia and USA**; International Date Line passes nearby.
Known as the **Key to the Mediterranean**.
Busiest strait connecting **Indian and Pacific Oceans**.
Shorter maritime route between **Europe and Asia** without going around Africa.

items.definition: Remember **UG-KG-D-C-S** -> **Uganda, Kenya, Gabon, Democratic Republic of Congo, Congo, Somalia, Sao Tome & Principe**.
Remember **P-A-N-I-S-E-A** -> **Pacific, Antarctic, North American, Indian, South American, Eurasian, African** plates.
Only **Europe and Asia (Eurasia)** contain completely landlocked sovereign states that do not touch open oceans.

items.term: Tropic of Capricorn Passes Through South America

items.definition: Australia is the smallest **continent**, but Greenland is the world's largest **island** (not a continent).
Mariana Trench is in the **Pacific Ocean**, NOT the Indian or Atlantic Ocean.
Antarctica has **no permanent human population**, only scientific research stations with rotational staff.
Arctic Ocean is surrounded by landmasses, but it is an **ocean basin**, not a sea or lake.
The Equator does **NOT** pass through mainland Australia; Australia lies entirely in the Southern Hemisphere.
Suez Canal connects the **Mediterranean Sea and Red Sea** (no locks), while Panama Canal connects the **Atlantic and Pacific Oceans** (uses locks).
Antarctica is technically the largest **desert** on Earth due to extremely low precipitation, not the Sahara.

upscNotes.content: Memorize the exact ranking of continents and oceans by area as UP Assistant Teacher exams frequently ask direct matching and ordering questions.
Do not confuse the deepest point of the world (Challenger Deep in Mariana Trench) with the longest mountain range (Andes on land, Mid-Oceanic Ridge underwater).
Pay special attention to straits connecting water bodies and separating landmasses, as map-based questions are heavily featured.
Remember that Europe and Asia are physically one continuous landmass (Eurasia), separated artificially by the Ural Mountains and Ural River for administrative and historical convenience.
Understand Alfred Wegener's evidence for Continental Drift: matching coastlines (Jigsaw fit), fossil distribution across oceans, and identical rock structures.

keyTakeaways: Earth's surface consists of **7 continents** and **5 major oceans**, with land concentrated predominantly in the Northern Hemisphere.
**Alfred Wegener's Continental Drift Theory** and **Plate Tectonics** explain the dynamic movement and shaping of continents and ocean basins.
The **Pacific Ocean** is the largest and deepest ocean, containing the Mariana Trench and the Pacific Ring of Fire.
Asia is the largest continent by area and population, while Australia is the smallest continent.
Strategic waterways like the **Suez Canal**, **Panama Canal**, and **Malacca Strait** are vital choke points for global trade and geopolitics.
Ocean relief features include continental shelves (rich in resources), abyssal plains, and deep-sea trenches.
